The global *DIgSILENT* library (`app.GetGlobalLibrary()`) holds the templates,
equipment types, dynamic models and reports that ship with *PowerFactory*.
Navigating it from a script is awkward because **the folder names shown in the
GUI are not the names the Python API expects**. In the GUI you see

```
Templates \ Grid-forming Converters \ WECC REGFM_A1 Droop Inverter - Storage
```

but `GetContents("Grid-forming Converters")` returns an empty list - the folder's
`loc_name` is actually `TemplGfc`, and the path the API needs is

```
Templ \ TemplGfc \ WECC REGFM_A1 Droop Inverter - Storage
```

This only affects the built-in *system* folders of the **global** library.
Folders and objects in your **user** account (and the templates themselves)
already have the name you see in the GUI, so there the Python API works as
expected and you can access objects as described in the [Getting Started](./getting_started.qmd) tutorial.

`powfacpy.applications.digsilent_library.DigsilentLibrary` bridges the gap: it
reads *PowerFactory*'s own localisation database from the installation folder
(`<install>\localisation\en-GB\data.db`) to translate the coded folder names, so
you can address library objects by the path shown in the GUI.

We first activate a *PowerFactory* project and create a `DigsilentLibrary` instance:

```{python}
import sys
import json

with open(r"..\..\settings_local.json") as settings_file:
    SETTINGS = json.load(settings_file)

sys.path.append(SETTINGS["local path to PowerFactory application"]) # e.g. r"C:\Program Files\DIgSILENT\PowerFactory 2025 SP5\Python\3.13"

import powerfactory

app = powerfactory.GetApplication()
app.Show()
app.ActivateProject(r"powfacpy\39_bus_with_der_copy_to_run_tests")

from powfacpy.applications.digsilent_library import DigsilentLibrary

lib = DigsilentLibrary(app)
```

# Resolving GUI paths

`get_object` walks the global library and matches each path segment against the
child objects' *displayed* names (and, as a fallback, their literal `loc_name`). That way you can use the GUI-style path as presented in the *Data Manager* of *PowerFactory*.
`"\\"` and `"/"` both work as separators.

![](.\figures\object-path-global-library.png)

```{python}
folder = lib.get_folder(r"Templates\Grid-forming Converters")
folder, folder.loc_name, folder.GetFullName()
```

```{python}
template = lib.get_template(
    r"Templates\Grid-forming Converters\WECC REGFM_A1 Droop Inverter - Storage"
)
template, template.GetClassName()
```

`get_folder` / `get_template` are `get_object` with a class check; use
`get_object` for anything else, and `error_if_non_existent=False` to get `None`
instead of an exception:

```{python}
lib.get_object(r"Templates\Does Not Exist", error_if_non_existent=False)
```

# Listing and translating

`list_contents` returns a `{displayed_name: object}` dictionary of a folder's
children; `list_templates` is the same, restricted to `IntTemplate`s:

```{python}
lib.list_templates(r"Templates\Grid-forming Converters")
```

```{python}
# every child of the folder, not just the templates
list(lib.list_contents("Templates").keys())
```

The dictionary keys are the names shown in the GUI. `gui_name` performs that
single-name translation and accepts either a coded `loc_name` or a folder
object:

```{python}
lib.gui_name("TemplGfc"), lib.gui_name(folder)
```

Only the built-in *system* folders carry a coded name that needs translating.
Anything that already has its GUI name - folders you created yourself, and the
templates themselves - is returned unchanged, so it is safe to call `gui_name`
on a name that is already "real":

```{python}
lib.gui_name("Grid-forming Converters"), lib.gui_name(template.loc_name)
```

The translations live in `folder_name_translations`, a `{loc_name: gui_name}`
dictionary read once (and cached) from *PowerFactory*'s localisation database
at `<install>\localisation\en-GB\data.db`:

```{python}
{k: lib.folder_name_translations[k] for k in ["Templ", "TemplGfc", "TemplPv", "TemplHvdc"]}
```

`gui_path` is the reverse of `get_object` - the full GUI-style path of any
library object:

```{python}
lib.gui_path(template)
```

# Checking the name table against your PowerFactory version

The translations come from a private *PowerFactory* file, so in principle they
could drift between versions. `unmapped_system_folders` walks the live library
and reports every *system* folder (`iopt_sys == 1`) below a given branch whose
`loc_name` has no entry in the name table:

```{python}
lib.unmapped_system_folders()  # within the 'Templates' branch by default
```

An empty list means the name table and this *PowerFactory* installation agree,
and every folder in that branch can be reached by its GUI name. A non-empty
list is not a hard failure - navigation still works for those folders through
their literal `loc_name` - but `gui_name` and `gui_path` will keep showing the
coded name until the table is extended (either by a *PowerFactory* update or by
adding an entry to `_FALLBACK_FOLDER_NAMES`).

The check deliberately skips folders whose `loc_name` contains a space: a few
vendor sub-libraries such as `Templates\HVDC\Hitachi Energy` are marked as
system folders but already carry a human-readable name, and *PowerFactory*'s
coded keys never contain spaces.
